The Lord's words: ﴿on couches woven [with gold]﴾ ﴿reclining upon them, facing one another﴾.

As-Sururu (السُّرُرُ) is the plural of sarir (سَرِيرٌ, couch). Allah has explained that their couches are raised, in His words in Surat al-Ghashiyah: ﴿therein are raised couches﴾ [al-Kahf: 13]. His words, ﴿mawdunah﴾ (مَوْضُونَةٍ), mean woven with gold. Some say they are gold rods interlaced with pearls and rubies. Every weave that is tightly made, with its parts entering into one another, the Arabs call wad' (وَضْنًا), and what is woven with it they call mawdun and wadin (وَضِينًا). From this comes the coat of mail described as mawdunah, when its weave is tightly made and some of its rings enter into others.

From this is the saying of al-A'sha:

"And of the weaving of Dawud is a mawdunah, led along with the tribe, caravan after caravan."

And his saying also:

"A white one, like a nihy (a river or pool of water) that is mawdunah,
having a crest above the collar of the bodice."

Of this same kind is the naming of the girth (bitan) that is woven from straps, with some of them entering into others, as wadin.

From this is the saying of the rajiz (rajaz poet):

"To you it runs, its girth loose,
its foal lying across its belly,
differing from the religion of the Christians is its religion."

These adorned couches are the ones referred to by the term al-ara'ik (الأرائِكِ) in His words: ﴿reclining therein upon the couches﴾ [al-Kahf: 31], and His words: ﴿they and their spouses, in shade, reclining upon couches﴾ [Ya-Sin: 56]. His words in this noble verse, ﴿reclining﴾ (مُتَّكِئِينَ), are a circumstantial clause (ḥāl, a clause describing the state of the subject at the time of the action) from the pronoun in His words ﴿upon couches﴾. The implied meaning is: they are settled upon couches, in the state of reclining upon them.

What Allah, the Majestic and Exalted, mentioned in this noble verse, that they are upon couches ﴿facing one another﴾, meaning that some of them look at the faces of others, each facing the other with his face, has been made clear in other verses, such as His words in Surat al-Hijr: ﴿And We will remove whatever rancor is in their breasts, as brothers upon couches facing one another﴾ [al-Hijr: 47], and His words in Surat as-Saffat: ﴿For those will be a known provision, fruits, and they will be honored, in the Gardens of Bliss, upon couches facing one another﴾ [as-Saffat: 41–44].

(p-518) His saying, exalted is He: ﴿There will go around among them boys made eternal﴾.

We have already presented the verses that clarify this in Surah at-Tur, in the discussion of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And there will go around among them boys [attending] them, as if they were pearls well-protected﴾ [at-Tur: 24].

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 56, verse 18:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And a cup from a flowing spring﴾ ﴿Whose effect will neither give them headache nor will they be intoxicated thereby.﴾

We have already presented the verses that clarify this in Surat at-Tur, in the discussion of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿They will pass around among themselves a cup wherein there is no ill speech nor sinful talk﴾ [at-Tur: 23], and in Surat al-Ma'idah, in the discussion of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, intoxicants, gambling...﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 90] to the end of the verse.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 56, verse 20:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And fruit of what they choose﴾ ﴿and the flesh of birds of what they desire﴾.

We have already discussed this in surah al-Tur, in the discussion of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And We provided them with fruit and meat of what they desire﴾ [al-Waqi'ah: 22].

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 56, verse 22:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And theirs will be wide-eyed maidens (hur 'in)﴾ ﴿like hidden pearls (ka-amthal al-lu'lu' al-maknun)﴾.

We have already presented the verses that clarify this in Surat al-Baqarah, in the discussion of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And for them therein are spouses purified﴾ [al-Baqarah: 25], and in al-Saffat, in the discussion of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And with them are those restraining their glances, with wide, lovely eyes﴾ [al-Saffat: 48], and in other places besides these.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 56, verse 25:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿They will not hear therein any vain speech or sinful utterance﴾ ﴿but only the saying "Peace, peace."﴾

We have already discussed this at length, with clarification, in surah Maryam, in the discussion of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿They will not hear therein any vain speech, but only "Peace," and for them is their provision therein morning and evening﴾ [Maryam: 62]. There we discussed the exceptive (al-istithna' al-munqati', the "disjunct exception," i.e. where what follows "illa" is not of the same kind as what precedes it), mentioned its evidences from the Qur'an and from the speech of the Arabs, and explained the views of the scholars of knowledge regarding its legal ruling (hukm).

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 56, verse 30:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And shade extended﴾ ﴿and water poured out﴾ ﴿and fruit abundant﴾ ﴿neither cut off nor forbidden﴾.

As for His saying ﴿And shade extended﴾, we have already presented the verses that clarify it in Surat an-Nisa' in our discussion of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And We will admit them to shade extending﴾ [an-Nisa': 57]. As for His saying ﴿and water poured out﴾ (p-519), it is indicated by many verses of the Book of Allah,

- such as His saying, exalted is He: ﴿In it are rivers of water unaltered﴾ [Muhammad: 15],

- and His saying: ﴿Indeed, the righteous will be within gardens and springs﴾ [al-Hijr: 45],

- and His saying: ﴿And the companions of the Fire will call out to the companions of Paradise, "Pour upon us some water"...﴾ the verse [al-A'raf: 50],

along with other verses.

Al-maskub is a passive participle (ism maf'ul) from sakaba the water and the like, when one pours it abundantly. The exegetes say that the rivers of Paradise flow without a trench, and that the water reaches them wherever they are, however they wish, as He, exalted is He, said: ﴿A spring from which the servants of Allah drink; they make it gush forth in abundance﴾ [al-Insan: 6]. As for His saying ﴿and fruit abundant﴾, we have already presented the verses that clarify it in Surat at-Tur in our discussion of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And We will provide them with fruit and meat from whatever they desire﴾ [at-Tur: 22].

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 56, verse 35:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, We have created them with a special creation﴾ ﴿and made them virgins﴾ ﴿loving, of equal age﴾ ﴿for the companions of the right hand﴾.

The pronoun in "ansha'nahunna" (We created them): some scholars said it refers to something previously mentioned, while other scholars said it refers to something not mentioned, though the context indicates it.

As for those who said it refers to something mentioned, they said it refers to His saying: ﴿and raised couches﴾. They said: because the intended meaning of "furush" (couches) is women, and the Arabs call a woman a garment (libas), a waist-wrapper (izar), a bed (firash), and a shoe (na'l). On this view, the intended meaning of "raised" (marfu'ah) in His saying is the raising of rank and station.

As for those who said it refers to something not mentioned, they said: it refers to women who were not mentioned, but the mention of the couches indicates them, because they recline upon them with their husbands.

Some scholars said: the intended meaning is the Houris (huur 'in), and whoever said this relied on His saying: ﴿Indeed, We have created them with a special creation﴾, because "insha'" (creation) is innovation and origination.

A group of scholars said: the intended meaning is the daughters of Adam who were in this world as old women, white-haired and bleary-eyed, and reports traced back to the Prophet (ﷺ) have come concerning this. According to this view, the meaning of ﴿We created them with a special creation﴾ is: We created them with a new creation.

His saying, exalted is He: "and made them" means: We made them "virgins" (abkar), which is the plural of bikr (virgin), the opposite of thayyib (non-virgin).

His saying: "'urub" (loving) — most of the seven readers, other than Hamzah and Shu'bah from 'Asim, read "'uruban" (p-520) with a damma on the 'ayn and the ra'. Hamzah and Shu'bah read "'urban" with a sukun on the ra', which is the dialect of Tamim. The meaning of both readings is one: it is the plural of 'arub, who is the woman who is lovingly devoted to her husband and good in her conduct toward him (husn al-tabu'ul), and this is the view of the majority. It is the correct view, God willing.

From this is the saying of Labid:

"And in the tent is an 'arub, not indecent, plump of buttocks, the gaze is blocked from her."

His saying, exalted is He: "atrab" (of equal age) is the plural of tirb, with a kasra on the ta', and tirb means peer of the same age (lidda). Its clarification is that a person's tirb is whoever was born with him at the same time, and its meaning in the verse is that the women of the people of Paradise are of one age, so there is among them no young woman and old woman, but they are all of one age, in the utmost of youth.

Some scholars say: they will be raised up equal in age, according to the age of thirty-three years, and reports transmitted from the Prophet (ﷺ) have come concerning this. That "atrab" means equal in age is well known in the speech of the Arabs.

From this is the saying of 'Umar ibn Abi Rabi'ah:

"They displayed her like a gazelle strutting between five maidens with swelling breasts, of equal age."

These three attributes contained in this noble verse are among the qualities of the women of the people of Paradise, and they have been clarified in other verses.

As for their being virgins on the Day of Resurrection, He clarified it in Surat al-Rahman in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿No human has touched them before them, nor any jinn﴾ [al-Rahman: 56, 74], in both places, because His saying ﴿No human has touched them before them, nor any jinn﴾ is an explicit text that their virginity does not cease.

As for their being 'urub, meaning loving toward their husbands, this is indicated by His saying in as-Saffat: ﴿And with them are women restraining their gaze, with large, lovely eyes﴾ [as-Saffat: 48], because its meaning is that they restrain their gaze to their husbands, not looking at others, due to the intensity of their love for them and their contentment with them, as we previously explained. And there is no doubt that a woman who does not look at anyone other than her husband is lovingly devoted to him and good in her conduct with him.

As for His saying in Sad: ﴿And with them are women restraining their gaze, of equal age﴾ [Sad: 52], and His saying in ar-Rahman: ﴿In them are women restraining their gaze, whom no human has touched before them, nor any jinn﴾ [ar-Rahman: 56], (p-521) as for their being of equal age, He clarified it in His saying in this verse of Sad: ﴿And with them are women restraining their gaze, of equal age﴾, and in Surat an-Naba in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, for the righteous is a place of triumph﴾ ﴿gardens and grapevines﴾ ﴿and maidens of equal age﴾ [an-Naba: 31-33].

His saying, exalted is He, in this noble verse: ﴿for the companions of the right hand﴾ is connected to His saying: ﴿Indeed, We have created them﴾. And His saying: ﴿and made them﴾ means: We created them and made them virgins for the companions of the right hand.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on Surah al-Waqi'ah (56), verse 41:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And the companions of the left hand—what are the companions of the left hand?﴾ ﴿In scorching wind and boiling water﴾ ﴿And a shade of black smoke﴾.

We have already explained the meaning of "the companions of the left hand" in this noble surah. We also clarified the meaning of *al-samum* (scorching wind) in the verses where it is mentioned in Surat al-Tur, in our discussion of His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿So Allah has been gracious to us and has protected us from the punishment of the scorching wind﴾ [al-Tur: 27].

We have also previously explained the attributes of the shade of the people of the Fire and the shade of the people of Paradise in Surat al-Nisa', in our discussion of His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And We will admit them to a shade, deep and extending﴾ [al-Nisa': 57]. There we clarified that the attributes of the shade of the people of the Fire are those mentioned in His saying here: ﴿And a shade of black smoke﴾ ﴿neither cool nor pleasant﴾ [al-Waqi'ah: 43–44], and in His saying in Surat al-Mursalat: ﴿Proceed to a shade having three branches﴾ ﴿Neither providing shade nor averting from the blaze﴾ [al-Mursalat: 30–31].

As for His saying ﴿min yahmum﴾ (of black smoke), it means: of very intensely black smoke. The form of *al-yahmum* is *yafʿul* (يَفْعُولُ). Its root is from *al-humam* (الحُمَم), which is charcoal, and it was said that it is derived from *al-ḥamm* (الحَمّ), which is blackened fat, blackened by its burning in the fire.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, they were before that affluent,﴾ ﴿and they used to persist in the great violation.﴾

We have already discussed this in Surat al-Tur, in the commentary on His saying, exalted is He: ﴿They said, "Indeed, we were before this, among our people, fearful. So Allah conferred favor upon us..."﴾ [al-Tur: 26-27], the verse.

**Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 56, verse 47:**

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And they used to say, "When we have died and become dust and bones, shall we indeed be resurrected?"﴾

When He, exalted and majestic, mentioned the punishment prepared for the companions of the left, He explained some of its causes. Among them, He mentioned that before this, in the worldly life, they were *mutrafun* (ﻣﺘﺮﻓﻴﻦ), meaning living in luxury and ease. We have already stated that the Qur'an indicates that indulgence, luxury and joy in this world are among the causes of punishment on the Day of Resurrection, because the one who indulges is turned away from God and does not believe in Him or in His messengers, as this noble verse indicates. His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So he will call for destruction﴾ ﴿and will enter the Blaze﴾ ﴿Indeed, he was among his people, joyful﴾ [Al-Inshiqaq: 11–13], and we have clarified this in our discussion of the verse of at-Tur mentioned a little earlier. (p-522)

As for what this noble verse indicates, namely that denying the resurrection is a cause of entering the Fire: when He mentioned that they were in scorching wind, boiling water and the shade of black smoke, He explained that among the causes of this is that they said, ﴿When we have died and become dust and bones﴾. This has been made clear in many verses, such as His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And if you are amazed, then amazing is their saying, "When we have become dust, will we indeed be in a new creation?" Those are the ones who disbelieved in their Lord, and those will have shackles around their necks, and those are the companions of the Fire; they will abide therein forever﴾ [Ar-Ra'd: 5].

We have already presented the verses that clarify this in Surat al-Furqan, in our discussion of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And We have prepared for those who deny the Hour a blaze﴾ [Al-Furqan: 11]. As for what He, exalted is He, mentioned in this noble verse of their denial of the resurrection of their earliest forefathers, in His saying: ﴿And our earliest forefathers?﴾ [Al-Waqi'ah: 48], and that He, exalted is He, made clear to them that He will resurrect the earliest and the last in His saying: ﴿Say, "Indeed, the earliest and the last﴾ ﴿will surely be gathered to the appointed time of a known day"﴾ [Al-Waqi'ah: 49–50], this has been made clear in other than this place. We explained therein that the resurrection they denied will indeed occur while they are humiliated and abased. This is in His saying, exalted is He, in as-Saffat: ﴿And they say, "This is not but obvious magic.﴾ ﴿When we have died and become dust and bones, will we indeed be resurrected?﴾ ﴿And our forefathers, the earliest?﴾ ﴿Say, "Yes, and you will be humbled."﴾ ﴿It will be but one shout, and at once they will be looking﴾ [As-Saffat: 15–19].

As for His saying, ﴿And our earliest forefathers?﴾, it was read by the majority of the Seven Readers (as-Sab'ah, the seven canonical readers), except Ibn 'Amir and Qalun on the authority of Nafi', who read *a-wa-ābā'unā* with a fatha on the waw, as an interrogative and a conjunction. We have already stated several times that when the interrogative hamzah (*hamzat al-istifham*, the question particle) is followed by a conjunctive particle such as the waw, the fa' or thumma, as in ﴿a-wa-ābā'unā?﴾, ﴿afa-amina ahlu al-qura?﴾ [Al-A'raf: 97], and ﴿a-thumma idha ma waqa'?﴾ [Yunus: 51], there are two views among the scholars of Arabic grammar and the exegetes:

The first of them is that the conjunctive particle links the sentence introduced by the interrogative to what precedes it, while the interrogative hamzah is ranked after the conjunction in grammatical order, but it has been placed before it in pronunciation, not in meaning, because the original position of the interrogative is at the beginning, as is known in its proper place.

The meaning according to this is clear: they denied their own resurrection with the particle of denial, which is the hamzah, and they joined to that, by the waw, their denial of the resurrection of their earliest forefathers, with the particle of denial, which is the hamzah placed before its original position in pronunciation but not in rank. (p-523) This view is the view of the earlier scholars of Arabic, and Abu Hayyan chose it in *al-Bahr al-Muhit*, and Ibn Hisham in *Mughni al-Labib*, and it is the one toward which we have come to lean recently, after we had leaned toward other views.

The second view: the interrogative hamzah is in its original position, and it is connected to a deleted sentence, and the sentence introduced by the interrogative is joined to the deleted sentence by the conjunctive particle that comes after the hamzah. This view is the one al-Zamakhshari leans toward in most places of his *Kashshaf*, though he sometimes leans toward other views.

According to this view, the estimate is: "Will we be resurrected, we and our earliest forefathers?"

What al-Zamakhshari mentioned here, that His saying "our forefathers" is conjoined to the waw of nominative in His saying "will be resurrected," and that conjoining to a connected pronoun of nominative without emphasis by a separate pronoun was permitted because of the separation by the hamzah, is not correct. Abu Hayyan, Ibn Hisham and others have refuted him on this.

This last view is the one toward which Ibn Malik leaned in *al-Khulasah*, in his saying:

*"And omitting a governing word that appears here, you may permit; and your conjoining a verb to a verb is correct."*

Qalun and Ibn 'Amir read this letter *aw ābā'unā* (or our forefathers) with the waw sukun. What appears to me, on their reading "aw" (or) with the meaning of the conjunctive waw, is that His saying "our forefathers" is conjoined to the position of the accusative which is the noun of *inna* (indeed), because conjoining a nominative to the accusative of *inna* after mentioning its predicate is permissible without dispute, since its subject, although accusative, is originally nominative, being originally a subject (mubtada'), as Ibn Malik said in *al-Khulasah*:

*"And your conjoining a nominative to the accusative of inna is permissible, after you have completed it."*

We said that "aw" has the meaning of the waw because its coming with the meaning of the waw is well known in the Qur'an and in the speech of the Arabs. Among its occurrences in the Qur'an is: ﴿So those who bring reminders﴾ ﴿as an excuse or a warning﴾ [Al-Mursalat: 5–6]; for the reminder is delivered as an excuse and a warning together, not as one or the other, because the meaning is that they came as a reminder by way of excuse and warning. And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And do not obey from among them a sinner or a disbeliever﴾ [Al-Insan: 24], meaning and a disbeliever. It is very common in the speech of the Arabs. Among it is the saying of 'Amr ibn Ma'di Karib:

*"A people who, when they hear the cry for help, you see them between one who bridles his horse and one who seizes its forelock."*

(p-524) The meaning is: between one who bridles his horse and one who seizes its forelock, i.e., one who takes hold of its forelock in order to bridle it. And the saying of Nabigha Dhubyani:

*"She said, 'Would that this pigeon, along with half of it, were to my pigeon, so the count would be complete.'*

*So they counted it and found it, as she claimed, sixty-six, neither less nor more."*

So his saying "aw nisfuhu" (or half of it) means "wa nisfuhu" (and half of it), as is clear from the meaning of the two verses mentioned, because what she intended was that she wished the pigeon passing by her, together with half of it, to be with her and her pigeon, so that all together would be a hundred pigeons. They found it sixty-six, and half of that is thirty-three, so the total would be ninety-nine. What is narrated from her about this is that she said:

*"Would that the pigeon were to its pigeon,*
*and half of it, a pair,*
*so the pigeons would be a hundred."*

And the saying of Tawbah ibn al-Humayyir:

*"Layla has claimed that I am a sinner,*
*either her piety is for my soul, or her sins are against it."*

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿When we have died and become dust and bones, will we indeed be resurrected?﴾ The majority of the readers agreed on affirming the interrogative hamzah in His saying ﴿When we have died﴾, and the majority of the Seven also affirmed it in His saying "a-inna" (will we indeed), except Nafi' and al-Kisa'i. Nafi' and al-Kisa'i read "inna lamab'ūthūn" (indeed we will be resurrected) with a single kasra hamzah, as a statement, as the author of *ad-Durar al-Lawami'* established in the basis of the reading of the Imam Nafi', with his saying:

*"A separation: if the interrogative occurs twice, make the second of them a statement.*
*And reverse it in an-Naml and above ar-Rum ... etc."*

The readings concerning the two hamzahs in *a-idha* and *a-inna* are well known. Nafi' softens the second hamzah between-between (*bayn bayn*, an intermediate sound between hamzah and the vowel). The transmission of Qalun from him is inserting an alif between the two hamzahs, the first being fully pronounced and the second softened.

The transmission of Qalun from Nafi' with softening and insertion corresponds to the reading of Abu 'Amr. Abu 'Amr and Qalun from Nafi' soften and insert. The transmission of Warsh from Nafi' is softening the latter of the two between-between without inserting an alif. This is the reading of Ibn Kathir and Warsh; so Ibn Kathir and Warsh soften and do not insert.

(p-525) Hisham from Ibn 'Amir read with both hamzahs fully pronounced, with the alif of insertion between them.

'Asim, Hamzah, al-Kisa'i and Ibn Dhakwan from Ibn 'Amir read with both hamzahs fully pronounced, without the alif of insertion. These are the correct readings in cases like *a-idha* and *a-inna* and similar ones in the Qur'an.

**Warning:**

Know, may God grant success to me and to you, that what has occurred in the African regions, of replacing the last of this hamzah and similar ones in the Qur'an with a pure *ha'* (h), is among the most abominable of wrongs and the greatest of falsehoods. It is a violation of the sanctity of the Great Qur'an and a transgression of the limits of God. No one is excused in this except the ignorant who does not know, who thinks that reading with a pure *ha'* is correct. We say this because replacing the hamzah in what has been mentioned with a pure *ha'* has not been related by anyone from the Messenger of God (ﷺ), nor did Gabriel ever descend with it at all, nor has it been narrated from any Companion, nor did any of the reciters read with it, and it is not permissible under any circumstances. Presumptuousness against God by adding a letter to His Book, namely this *ha'* with which the angel never descended from heaven at all, is as you see. That the Arabic language has heard the replacement of hamzah with *ha'* does not justify presumption against God by inserting into His Book a letter that neither God nor His Messenger permitted.

The claim that the practice has gone on with the reading with *ha'* is not to be relied upon, because the continuation of practice in falsehood is falsehood, and there is no precedent in falsehood by the consensus of the Muslims. Precedent is only in what is true, and the recitation is a followed sunnah, transmitted from the Messenger of God (ﷺ), and there is no disagreement about this.

His saying, exalted is He: "mitna" (we have died). It was read by Ibn 'Amir, Ibn Kathir, Abu 'Amr and Shu'bah from 'Asim as "mutna" with a *damma* on the mim. It was read by Nafi', Hamzah, al-Kisa'i and Hafs from 'Asim as "mitna" with a *kasra* on the mim. We have already mentioned the justification for the kasra of the mim as a dialectal form in Surat Maryam, in our discussion of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Oh, I wish I had died before this﴾ [Maryam: 23].

Al-Shinqiti's commentary on surah 56, verse 51:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Then indeed you, O you who are astray and deniers,﴾ ﴿will surely eat from a tree of zaqqum,﴾ ﴿and fill your bellies with it,﴾ ﴿and drink on top of it from scalding water,﴾ ﴿and drink like the drinking of camels afflicted with thirst.﴾

We have already given an explanation and clarification of this in surah As-Saffat, in discussing His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Then indeed for them after it is a mixture of scalding water,﴾ [As-Saffat: 67].

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 56, verse 56:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿This is their nuzul (hospitality) on the Day of Recompense﴾.

Nuzul (with two dammas, nuzul) is the provision of a guest, which is offered to him upon his arrival as an honour to him. From it is the saying of the Exalted: ﴿Indeed, those who believed and did righteous deeds, for them will be the Gardens of Paradise as a nuzul﴾ [al-Kahf: 107]. The Arabs sometimes use nuzul in the opposite sense, by way of mockery and contempt, and the Qur'an has used nuzul for what is offered to the people of the Fire of punishment, as in His saying here, concerning their punishment mentioned in His saying: ﴿Indeed, you will surely eat from a tree of zaqqum﴾ up to His saying: ﴿drinking like thirsty camels﴾, ﴿This is their nuzul﴾ [al-Waqi'ah: 52–56], meaning: this punishment mentioned is their hospitality and their provision offered to them upon their arrival in their abode, which is the Fire, just as He said, the Exalted, to the contemptible, humiliated disbeliever: ﴿Taste! Indeed, you are the mighty, the noble﴾ [al-Dukhan: 49].

What this noble verse contains of applying nuzul to the punishment of the people of the Fire is explained (p-527) in other places, such as His saying at the end of this noble surah: ﴿But for him is a nuzul of boiling water, and burning in Hellfire﴾ [al-Waqi'ah: 93–94], and His saying, the Exalted, at the end of al-Kahf: ﴿Indeed, We have prepared Hell for the disbelievers as a nuzul﴾ [al-Kahf: 102]. A parallel to this in Arabic speech is the saying of Abu al-Sa'd al-Dabbi:

"And we, whenever the tyrant came to us with his army as a guest, made spears and keen swords his nuzul."

His saying: Yawm al-Din, meaning the Day of Recompense, as has been mentioned repeatedly before.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 56, verse 57:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿We created you, so why do you not believe?﴾

When the disbelievers denied their resurrection and that of their earlier forefathers, and Allah commanded His Messenger to inform them that He, exalted is He, will resurrect all of the earlier and later generations, and mentioned the recompense of those who deny the resurrection, which is eating the zaqqum (a bitter tree of Hellfire) and drinking boiling water (hamim), He followed that with the decisive proofs that indicate the resurrection, saying: ﴿We created you﴾ this first creation ﴿so why do you not believe?﴾, meaning: so why do you not believe in the resurrection, which is the second creation? For the re-creation cannot be more difficult than the initial creation, as is well known.

This proof for the resurrection, by means of the first creation indicating the second creation, has been clarified in very many verses,

- such as His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And it is He who begins creation and then repeats it, and that is easier for Him﴾ [al-Rum: 27],
- and His saying: ﴿As We began the first creation, We will repeat it; a promise upon Us. Indeed, We are ever doing it﴾ [al-Anbiya: 104],
- and His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿O mankind, if you are in doubt about the resurrection, then indeed We created you from dust﴾ [al-Hajj: 5],
- and His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Say, "He will give them life who produced them the first time"﴾ [Ya-Sin: 79],
- and His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿They will say, "Who will return us?" Say, "He who created you the first time"﴾ [al-Isra: 51].

Verses of this kind are numerous and well known. We have mentioned them with clarification and abundance in many places of this blessed Book, in the surahs al-Baqarah, al-Nahl, al-Hajj, al-Jathiyah, and other places, and we have referred to them frequently.

As for His saying, may He be exalted, in this noble verse: ﴿so why do you not believe?﴾, "lawla" is a particle of tahdid (urging and reproach), and its meaning is a demand made with urgency and intensity. So the verse indicates the intensity of Allah's urging the disbelievers and exhorting them to affirm the resurrection, because of the manifestness of its decisive proof, which is His creating them in the first place.

**Allah's statement:** ﴿Have you considered that which you emit?﴾ ﴿Is it you who create it, or are We the Creators?﴾

We have already mentioned shortly before this the statements of the scholars concerning the interrogative hamza (hamzat al-istifham, the hamza of interrogation) that is followed by a conjunction particle, and we have mentioned it several times before this. Allah's statement ﴿Have you considered that which you emit?﴾ means: have you considered what you pour out of semen into the wombs of women? The word "mā" (ما) is a relative pronoun, the verbal clause is the relative clause (ṣilat al-mawṣūl), and the returning pronoun to the antecedent is omitted, because it is in the accusative governed by a verb. The full construction is: "have you considered that which you emit it." The Arabs say amnā al-nuṭfah (أمنى النطفة), in the quadriliteral form, yumnīhā (يمنيها) with the prefixed vowel of the present tense, when he poured it into the womb of the woman. From this is Allah's statement ﴿from a drop of semen when it is emitted﴾ [an-Najm: 46]. And manā yamnā (مَنَى يَمْنَى), in the triliteral form, is a sound dialect, except that reciting with it is irregular (shādh).

Among those who read tumnūna (تَمْنُونَ) with a fatḥah on the tā' as a present-tense triliteral form (from the unaugmented root) are Abū as-Sammāl and Ibn as-Samayqa'. Allah's statement ﴿Is it you who create it, or are We the Creators?﴾ is an interrogation of affirmation (istifhām taqrīr), for they must say: "You are the creators." It is then said to them: if We created this human, the clear adversary, from that drop which is emitted into the womb, then how do you deny Our power to create him again, while you know that re-creation cannot be more difficult than the initial creation? The pronoun in the accusative in "takhluqūnahu" (تَخْلُقُونَهُ) returns to the relative antecedent, meaning: you create that which you emit of drops, as clots (ʿalaqan), then as lumps of flesh (muḍghan), up to its last stages.

What this verse contains of decisive proofs of the perfection of Allah's power over resurrection and other matters, and that He alone is the one worthy of worship, by explaining the stages of human creation, has come clarified in other verses. We have already discussed this fully with the Qur'anic verses, and we explained what relates to each of its stages of legal rulings in Surat al-Ḥajj, in the commentary on His statement ﴿O mankind, if you are in doubt about the resurrection, indeed We created you from dust﴾ [al-Ḥajj: 5], and the verse.

We also mentioned the stages of human creation in Surat ar-Raḥmān, in the commentary on His statement ﴿He created man﴾ ﴿and taught him eloquence﴾ [ar-Raḥmān: 3–4], and in other places.

We have also clarified the verses indicating the stages of his creation, in general and in detail, in (the commentary on) al-Ḥajj.

**Caution (tanbīh):**

This proof indicating resurrection, which is the creation of man from a drop of emitted semen, is obligatory for every person to reflect upon, because Allah, the Majestic and Exalted, directed the command to reflect upon it to the semen of man. The basic meaning of the imperative form, by strict verification, is obligation, unless there is a clear indication diverting it from that. This is the case in His statement ﴿So let man look at what he was created from﴾ ﴿He was created from a gushing fluid﴾ [aṭ-Ṭāriq: 5–6]. We have already explained it at the beginning of Surat an-Naḥl.

Nāfiʿ read this word ʾafara'aytum (أَفَرَأَيْتُمْ) with the hamza after the rāʾ softened (tashīl), between-between (bayna bayn).

The well-known transmission on which the recitation from Warsh from him is based is replacing the hamza with an alif and prolonging it (ishbāʿ), because the yāʾ after it is silent.

al-Kisāʾī read ʾafaraytum (أَفَرَيْتُمْ) with the hamza omitted. The rest of the Seven read it with the hamza made clear (taḥqīq).

Allah's statement ﴿ʾa-ʾantum﴾ (أأنتم) was read by Nāfiʿ, Ibn Kathīr, Abū ʿAmr, and Hishām from Ibn ʿĀmir in one of the two transmissions, with the second hamza softened (tashīl). The well-known transmission on which the recitation from Warsh from Nāfiʿ is based is replacing the second hamza with an alif, prolonged (ishbāʿ) because the nūn after it is silent. ʿĀṣim, Ḥamzah, al-Kisāʾī, and Hishām from Ibn ʿĀmir in the other transmission read it with both hamzahs made clear. Qālūn, Abū ʿAmr, and Hishām read it with the alif of insertion (alif al-idkhāl) between the two hamzahs, and the rest read it without it.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 56, verse 60:

قَوْلُهُ تَعالى: ﴿نَحْنُ قَدَّرْنا بَيْنَكُمُ المَوْتَ وما نَحْنُ بِمَسْبُوقِينَ﴾ ﴿عَلى أنْ نُبَدِّلَ أمْثالَكم ونُنْشِئَكم في ما لا تَعْلَمُونَ﴾.

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿We have decreed death among you, and We are not to be outdone﴾ ﴿in replacing your likenesses and bringing you into being in what you do not know﴾.

قَرَأ هَذا الحَرْفَ عامَّةُ القُرّاءِ السَّبْعَةِ غَيْرَ ابْنِ كَثِيرٍ قَدَّرْنا بِتَشْدِيدِ الدّالِّ، وقَرَأهُ ابْنُ كَثِيرٍ بِتَخْفِيفِها، وقَدْ قَدَّمْنا في تَرْجَمَةِ هَذا الكِتابِ المُبارَكِ أنَّ الآيَةَ الكَرِيمَةَ قَدْ يَكُونُ فِيها وجْهانِ أوْ أكْثَرُ مِنَ التَّفْسِيرِ، ويَكُونُ كُلُّ ذَلِكَ صَحِيحًا، وكُلُّهُ يَشْهَدُ لَهُ قُرْآنٌ، فَنَذْكُرُ الجَمِيعَ وأدِلَّتَهُ مِنَ القُرْآنِ، ومِن ذَلِكَ هَذِهِ الآيَةِ الكَرِيمَةِ.

The majority of the seven readers (al-qurra' al-sab'ah, the seven canonical reciters), except Ibn Kathir, read this word as qaddarna with a shaddah on the dal, while Ibn Kathir read it with the dal unstressed. We have already mentioned in the introduction to this blessed book that a noble verse may have two or more interpretations (tafsir), all of which are valid and all of which are supported by the Qur'an. So we will mention them all along with their Qur'anic evidence, and this noble verse is one of them.

وَإيضاحُ ذَلِكَ أنَّ قَوْلَهُ: قَدَّرْنا [الواقعة: ٦٠] وجْهانِ مِنَ التَّفْسِيرِ، وفِيما تَتَعَلَّقُ بِهِ: ﴿عَلى أنْ نُبَدِّلَ﴾ [الواقعة: ٦١] وجْهانِ أيْضًا، فَقالَ بَعْضُ العُلَماءِ: وهو اخْتِيارُ ابْنِ جَرِيرٍ أنَّ قَوْلَهُ: ﴿قَدَّرْنا بَيْنَكُمُ المَوْتَ﴾ أيْ قَدَّرْنا لِمَوْتِكم آجالًا مُخْتَلِفَةً وأعْمارًا مُتَفاوِتَةً فَمِنكم مَن يَمُوتُ صَغِيرًا ومِنكم مَن يَمُوتُ شابًّا، ومِنكم مَن يَمُوتُ شَيْخًا.

The clarification of this is that His saying qaddarna [al-Waqi'ah: 60] has two interpretations, and what it relates to, ﴿in replacing your likenesses﴾ [al-Waqi'ah: 61], also has two interpretations. Some scholars said, and this is the preference of Ibn Jarir, that His saying ﴿We have decreed death among you﴾ means: We have decreed for your deaths different terms and varying lifespans; so among you is one who dies young, among you is one who dies as a youth, and among you is one who dies as an elder.

وَهَذا المَعْنى دَلَّتْ عَلَيْهِ آياتٌ كَثِيرَةٌ مِن كِتابِ اللَّهِ

This meaning is indicated by many verses of the Book of God, such as:

• كَقَوْلِهِ تَعالى: ﴿ثُمَّ نُخْرِجُكم طِفْلًا ثُمَّ لِتَبْلُغُوا أشُدَّكم ومِنكم مَن يُتَوَفّى ومِنكم مَن يُرَدُّ إلى أرْذَلِ العُمُرِ﴾ [الحج: ٥]،

• His saying: ﴿Then We bring you forth as infants, then that you may reach your maturity; and among you is one who is taken in death, and among you is one who is returned to the most abject age﴾ [al-Hajj: 5],

• وقَوْلِهِ تَعالى: ﴿ثُمَّ لِتَكُونُوا شُيُوخًا ومِنكم مَن يُتَوَفّى مِن قَبْلُ ولِتَبْلُغُوا أجَلًا مُسَمًّى ولَعَلَّكم تَعْقِلُونَ﴾ [غافر: ٦٧]،

• His saying: ﴿Then that you may become elders—and among you is one who dies before that—and that you may reach an appointed term, and perhaps you will understand﴾ [Ghafir: 67],

• وقَوْلِهِ تَعالى: ﴿وَما يُعَمَّرُ مِن مُعَمَّرٍ ولا يُنْقَصُ مِن عُمُرِهِ إلّا في كِتابٍ﴾ [فاطر: ١١]،

• His saying: ﴿No one is granted a long life, nor is his life shortened, except that it is in a Book﴾ [Fatir: 11],

• وقَوْلِهِ تَعالى: ﴿وَلَنْ يُؤَخِّرَ اللَّهُ نَفْسًا إذا جاءَ أجَلُها﴾ [المنافقون: ١١]،

• His saying: ﴿And God will never delay a soul when its term has come﴾ [al-Munafiqun: 11],

• وقَوْلِهِ: (p-٥٣٠)﴿وَما نَحْنُ بِمَسْبُوقِينَ﴾ [الواقعة: ٦]،

• and His saying: (p-530) ﴿and We are not to be outdone﴾ [al-Waqi'ah: 60],

أيْ ما نَحْنُ بِمَغْلُوبِينَ. والعَرَبُ تَقُولُ: سَبَقَهُ عَلى كَذا أيْ غَلَبَهُ عَلَيْهِ وأعْجَزَهُ عَنْ إدْراكِهِ، أيْ: وما نَحْنُ بِمَغْلُوبِينَ عَلى ما قَدَّرْنا مِن آجالِكم وحَدَّدْناهُ مِن أعْمارِكم فَلا يَقْدِرُ أحَدٌ أنْ يُقَدِّمَ أجَلًا أخَّرْناهُ ولا يُؤَخِّرَ أجَلًا قَدَّمْناهُ.

That is, we are not overcome. The Arabs say sabaqahu 'ala kadha, meaning he overcame him in it and made him unable to reach it. That is: and We are not overcome in what We have decreed of your terms and determined of your lifespans, so no one can bring forward a term that We have deferred, nor defer a term that We have brought forward.

وَهَذا المَعْنى دَلَّتْ عَلَيْهِ آياتٌ كَثِيرَةٌ

This meaning is indicated by many verses, such as:

• كَقَوْلِهِ تَعالى: ﴿فَإذا جاءَ أجَلُهم لا يَسْتَأْخِرُونَ ساعَةً ولا يَسْتَقْدِمُونَ﴾ [الأعراف: ٣٤]،

• His saying: ﴿So when their term comes, they cannot delay it an hour, nor can they advance it﴾ [al-A'raf: 34],

• وقَوْلِهِ تَعالى: ﴿إنَّ أجَلَ اللَّهِ إذا جاءَ لا يُؤَخَّرُ﴾ [نوح: ٤]،

• His saying: ﴿Indeed, when the term of God comes, it is not deferred﴾ [Nuh: 4],

• وقَوْلِهِ تَعالى: ﴿وَما كانَ لِنَفْسٍ أنْ تَمُوتَ إلّا بِإذْنِ اللَّهِ كِتابًا مُؤَجَّلًا﴾ [آل عمران: ١٤٥]،

• His saying: ﴿And it is not for any soul to die except by God's permission, a decree with a specified term﴾ [Al 'Imran: 145],

إلى غَيْرِ ذَلِكَ مِنَ الآياتِ.

and other verses besides these.

وَعَلى هَذا القَوْلِ، فَقَوْلُهُ تَعالى: ﴿عَلى أنْ نُبَدِّلَ أمْثالَكُمْ﴾ [الواقعة: ٦١]، لَيْسَ مُتَعَلِّقًا بِـ ”مَسْبُوقِينَ“ بَلْ بِقَوْلِهِ تَعالى: ﴿نَحْنُ قَدَّرْنا بَيْنَكُمُ المَوْتَ﴾ [الواقعة: ٦٠]، والمَعْنى: نَحْنُ قَدَّرْنا بَيْنَكُمُ المَوْتَ عَلى أنْ نُبَدِّلَ أمْثالَكم، أيْ نُبَدِّلَ مِنَ الَّذِينَ ماتُوا أمْثالًا لَهم نُوجِدُهم.

According to this view, His saying ﴿in replacing your likenesses﴾ [al-Waqi'ah: 61] is not connected to "not to be outdone" but to His saying ﴿We have decreed death among you﴾ [al-Waqi'ah: 60]. The meaning is: We have decreed death among you on condition that We replace your likenesses, that is, We replace those who died with likenesses of them that We bring into being.

وَعَلى هَذا، فَمَعْنى تَبْدِيلِ أمْثالِهِمْ - إيجادُ آخَرِينَ مِن ذُرِّيَّةِ أُولَئِكَ الَّذِينَ ماتُوا، وهَذا المَعْنى تَشْهَدُ لَهُ آياتٌ مِن كِتابِ اللَّهِ كَقَوْلِهِ تَعالى: ﴿إنْ يَشَأْ يُذْهِبْكم ويَسْتَخْلِفْ مِن بَعْدِكم ما يَشاءُ كَما أنْشَأكم مِن ذُرِّيَّةِ قَوْمٍ آخَرِينَ﴾ [الأنعام: ١٣٣]، إلى غَيْرِ ذَلِكَ مِنَ الآياتِ.

On this view, the meaning of replacing their likenesses is the bringing into being of others from the offspring of those who died. This meaning is supported by verses of the Book of God, such as His saying: ﴿If He wills, He can remove you and bring in after you whom He wills, just as He produced you from the offspring of another people﴾ [al-An'am: 133], and other verses besides it.

وَهَذا التَّفْسِيرُ هو اخْتِيارُ ابْنِ جَرِيرٍ، وقِراءَةُ ”قَدَّرْنا“ بِالتَّشْدِيدِ مُناسِبَةٌ لِهَذا الوَجْهِ، وكَذَلِكَ لَفْظَةُ ”بَيْنَكُمُ“ .

This interpretation is the preference of Ibn Jarir, and the reading qaddarna with the shaddah suits this view, as does the word "among you" (baynakum).

الوَجْهُ الثّانِي: أنَّ ”قَدَّرْنا“ بِمَعْنى قَضَيْنا وكَتَبْنا أيْ كَتَبْنا المَوْتَ وقَدَّرْناهُ عَلى جَمِيعِ الخَلْقِ، وهَذا الوَجْهُ تَشْهَدُ لَهُ آياتٌ مِن كِتابِ اللَّهِ

The second interpretation: qaddarna means "We decided" and "We wrote," that is, We wrote death and decreed it upon all creation. This view is supported by verses of the Book of God, such as:

• كَقَوْلِهِ تَعالى: ﴿كُلُّ شَيْءٍ هالِكٌ إلّا وجْهَهُ﴾ [القصص: ٨٨]،

• His saying: ﴿Everything will perish except His Face﴾ [al-Qasas: 88],

• وقَوْلِهِ تَعالى: ﴿كُلُّ نَفْسٍ ذائِقَةُ المَوْتِ﴾ [الأنبياء: ٣٥]،

• His saying: ﴿Every soul will taste death﴾ [al-Anbiya': 35],

• وقَوْلِهِ تَعالى: ﴿وَتَوَكَّلْ عَلى الحَيِّ الَّذِي لا يَمُوتُ﴾ [الفرقان: ٥٨]، وعَلى هَذا القَوْلِ فَقَوْلُهُ: ﴿عَلى أنْ نُبَدِّلَ﴾ [الواقعة: ٦١]،

• His saying: ﴿And rely upon the Ever-Living who does not die﴾ [al-Furqan: 58]. On this view, His saying ﴿on condition that We replace﴾ [al-Waqi'ah: 61]

مُتَعَلِّقٌ بِـ ”مَسْبُوقِينَ“، أيْ: ما نَحْنُ مَغْلُوبِينَ، والمَعْنى: وما نَحْنُ بِمَغْلُوبِينَ عَلى أنْ نُبَدِّلَ أمْثالَكم إنْ أهْلَكْناكم لَوْ شِئْنا، فَنَحْنُ قادِرُونَ عَلى إهْلاكِكم، ولا يُوجَدُ أحَدٌ يَغْلِبُنا ويَمْنَعُنا مِن خَلْقِ أمْثالِكم بَدَلًا مِنكم.

is connected to "not to be outdone," that is: we are not overcome. The meaning is: and We are not overcome in replacing your likenesses, if We destroy you, were We to will it. We are able to destroy you, and no one can overcome Us or prevent Us from creating likenesses of you in your place.

وَهَذا المَعْنى تَشْهَدُ لَهُ آياتٌ مِن كِتابِ اللَّهِ

This meaning is supported by verses of the Book of God, such as:

• كَقَوْلِهِ تَعالى: ﴿إنْ يَشَأْ يُذْهِبْكم أيُّها النّاسُ ويَأْتِ بِآخَرِينَ وكانَ اللَّهُ عَلى ذَلِكَ قَدِيرًا﴾ [النساء: ١٣٣]،

• His saying: ﴿If He wills, He can remove you, O people, and bring others; and God is ever capable of that﴾ [al-Nisa': 133],

• وقَوْلِهِ تَعالى: ﴿إنْ يَشَأْ يُذْهِبْكم ويَسْتَخْلِفْ مِن بَعْدِكم ما يَشاءُ﴾ [الأنعام: ١٣٣]،

• His saying: ﴿If He wills, He can remove you and bring in after you whom He wills﴾ [al-An'am: 133],

• وقَوْلِهِ تَعالى: (p-٥٣١)﴿إنْ يَشَأْ يُذْهِبْكم ويَأْتِ بِخَلْقٍ جَدِيدٍ﴾ ﴿وَما ذَلِكَ عَلى اللَّهِ بِعَزِيزٍ﴾ [إبراهيم: ١٩ - ٢٠]،

• and His saying: (p-531) ﴿If He wills, He can remove you and bring a new creation﴾ ﴿And that is not difficult for God﴾ [Ibrahim: 19–20],

• وقَوْلِهِ تَعالى: ﴿وَإنْ تَتَوَلَّوْا يَسْتَبْدِلْ قَوْمًا غَيْرَكم ثُمَّ لا يَكُونُوا أمْثالَكُمْ﴾ [محمد: ٣٨]، وقَدْ قَدَّمْنا هَذا في سُورَةِ النِّساءِ في الكَلامِ عَلى قَوْلِهِ تَعالى: ﴿إنْ يَشَأْ يُذْهِبْكم أيُّها النّاسُ﴾ الآيَةَ [النساء: ١٣٣] . وقَوْلُهُ تَعالى في هَذِهِ الآيَةِ الكَرِيمَةِ: ﴿وَنُنْشِئَكم في ما لا تَعْلَمُونَ﴾ [الواقعة: ٦١]،

• and His saying: ﴿And if you turn away, He will substitute a people other than you, and they will not be like you﴾ [Muhammad: 38]. We have already mentioned this in surah al-Nisa' in the discussion of His saying ﴿If He wills, He can remove you, O people﴾ [al-Nisa': 133]. As for His saying in this noble verse: ﴿and bringing you into being in what you do not know﴾ [al-Waqi'ah: 61],

فِيهِ لِلْعُلَماءِ أقْوالٌ مُتَقارِبَةٌ.

scholars have several closely related views concerning it.

قالَ بَعْضُهم: ”نُنْشِئَكم“ بَعْدَ إهْلاكِكم فِيما لا تَعْلَمُونَهُ مِنَ الصُّوَرِ والهَيْئاتِ، كَأنْ نُنْشِئَكم قِرَدَةً وخَنازِيرَ، كَما فَعَلْنا بِبَعْضِ المُجْرِمِينَ قَبْلَكم.

Some said: "nunshi'akum" means after your destruction, in forms and shapes you do not know, such as bringing you into being as monkeys and pigs, just as We did with some criminals before you.

وَقالَ بَعْضُهم: ”نُنْشِئَكم“ فِيما لا تَعْلَمُونَهُ مِنَ الصِّفاتِ، فَنُغَيِّرَ صِفاتِكم ونُجَمِّلَ المُؤْمِنِينَ بِبَياضِ الوُجُوهِ، ونُقَبِّحَ الكافِرِينَ بِسَوادِ الوُجُوهِ وزُرْقَةِ العُيُونِ، إلى غَيْرِ ذَلِكَ مِنَ الأقْوالِ.

Others said: "nunshi'akum" means in attributes you do not know, so that We change your attributes, beautifying the believers with white faces, and making the disbelievers ugly with black faces and blue eyes, along with other sayings.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 56, verse 63:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Have you considered that which you plant?﴾ ﴿Is it you who make it grow, or are We the growers?﴾ ﴿If We willed, We would make it debris, and you would remain astonished﴾.

This noble verse contains a second decisive proof of the Resurrection and a great favour upon creation through the creation of their provision. His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Have you considered that which you plant?﴾ [al-Waqi'ah: 63] means: Have you considered the seed that you place in the earth after tilling it, i.e., stirring and levelling it? ﴿Is it you who make it grow?﴾ i.e., you make it into a crop, then you nurture it until it becomes mature and fit for eating, ﴿or are We the growers of it?﴾ There is no doubt that the answer, for which there is no other answer, is that it is said: You, O our Lord, are the Sower and the Causer of growth, and we have no power over that. So it is said to them: Every intelligent person knows that He who caused this ear of grain to grow from this seed that rotted in the depths of the earth is able to resurrect you after your death. That the growth of plants after their non-existence is among the proofs of the Resurrection has come explained in verses,

• such as His saying: ﴿And among His signs is that you see the earth humbled, but when We send down water upon it, it stirs and swells. Indeed, He who revives it is the Reviver of the dead﴾ [Fussilat: 39],

• and His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So look at the traces of Allah's mercy, how He revives the earth after its death. Indeed, that is the Reviver of the dead, and He is over all things Competent﴾ [al-Rum: 50],

• and His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Until, when they carry heavy clouds, We drive them to a dead land, and We send down water therewith and bring forth thereby fruits of every kind. Thus We bring forth the dead, that you may remember﴾ [al-A'raf: 57].

Verses of this kind are many and well known. We have already presented them in full, together with the rest of the verses on the proofs of the Resurrection, in many places in Surat al-Baqarah, al-Nahl, al-Jathiyah and other places, (p-532) and we have referred to them repeatedly.

Caution:

Know that every human being is obliged to reflect upon this proof indicated by this noble verse, because Allah, Majestic and Exalted, has directed in His Book a clear, general command, applying to everything that qualifies as a human being, to reflect upon this great proof, which includes a favour of the greatest blessings upon creation, and to show the greatness of Allah, His power over the Resurrection and other things, and the great need of His creatures for Him despite His independence of them. That is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So let man look at his food﴾ ﴿That We poured down water in torrents﴾ ﴿Then We split the earth in splitting﴾ ﴿And caused to grow therein grain﴾ ﴿And grapes and herbage﴾ ﴿And olives and palm trees﴾ ﴿And gardens dense﴾ ﴿And fruit and pasture﴾ ﴿As provision for you and your livestock﴾ [Abasa: 24–32].

The meaning: Look, O weak man, at your food, such as the bread you eat and cannot do without. Who created the water that became the means of its growth? Can anyone other than Allah create water, i.e., bring it forth from absolute non-existence into existence? Then suppose the water was created: can anyone other than Allah cause it to descend in this tremendous, mighty manner by which the earth is watered without destruction or drowning? Then suppose the water descended into the earth: who is able to split the earth so that the crop may pass through? Then suppose the crop came up: who is able to bring forth the ear from it? Then suppose the ear came out of it: who is able to cause the grain to grow within it and nurture it until it becomes ripe and fit for eating?

﴿Look at its fruit when it bears fruit, and at its ripening. Indeed, in that are signs for a people who believe﴾ [al-An'am: 99]. The meaning: Look at the fruit at the time it emerges, weak and not fit for eating, and look at its ripening, i.e., look at it after it has become ripe, mature and fit for eating; you will know that He who nurtured it and made it grow until it became as you see it at the time of its ripening is Competent over all things, and Bestower of great favour upon you. Therefore He said: ﴿Indeed, in that are signs for a people who believe﴾ [al-An'am: 99]. So it is necessary for man to contemplate, look at his food, and reflect.

His saying: ﴿Then We split the earth﴾ [Abasa: 25], i.e., splitting it for the plants, up to the end of what We have explained.

His saying, in this noble verse: ﴿If We willed, We would make it debris﴾ [al-Waqi'ah: 65], means: If We willed to smash that crop, We would make it debris, i.e., crumbs and stubble, but We did not do that out of mercy towards you. The object of the verb of willing is omitted because it is sufficiently indicated by the apodosis of the conditional, and its supposed form is as we mentioned. His saying: ﴿And you would remain astonished﴾ [al-Waqi'ah: 65] (p-533) some scholars said: the meaning is "you would remain amazed at the smashing of your crop."

Some scholars said: "astonished" (tafakkahun) means "regretful over what you lost of the expense upon it," like His saying: ﴿So he began to turn over his palms over what he had spent upon it﴾ [al-Kahf: 42].

Some scholars said: "you would be regretful over the disobedience of Allah which was the cause of the smashing of your crop." The first of the two views regarding the cause of the regret is the more apparent.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 56, verse 68:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Have you considered the water that you drink?﴾ ﴿Is it you who bring it down from the rain-cloud, or are We the ones who bring it down?﴾ ﴿If We willed, We could make it bitter; so why do you not give thanks?﴾

This noble verse includes a great favour from Him upon His creation through the water they drink. It is also one of His signs that indicate His greatness, the perfection of His power, and the intense need of His creation for Him. The meaning is: Have you considered the water that you drink, which you cannot do without for a single moment, and if We were to destroy it, you would all perish in the shortest time? ﴿Is it you who bring it down from the rain-cloud, or are We the ones who bring it down?﴾ [al-Waqi'ah: 69].

The answer that has no other answer is: You, O our Lord; it is You who bring it down from the rain-cloud, and we have no power to do that. So it is said to them: If you are in this degree of intense need for Him, exalted is He, then why do you disbelieve in Him, drink His water, eat His provision, and worship other than Him?

What this noble verse includes of the favour upon creation through water, and that they are obliged to believe in Allah and obey Him in gratitude for the blessing of this water, as He alluded to here in His saying: ﴿so why do you not give thanks?﴾ [al-Waqi'ah: 70], has come in other verses of the Book of Allah:

• As in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And We sent down water from the sky in measure, and We caused it to settle in the earth; and indeed, We are able to drain it away. Then We produced for you thereby gardens of palm trees and grapes...﴾ — [al-Hijr: 22] (correction: the verse is ﴿And We sent down from the sky water, and We gave it to you to drink, and you are not its keepers﴾ [al-Hijr: 22]),

• And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿It is He who sent down from the sky water; from it is drink for you, and from it are trees in which you pasture [your animals]﴾ [al-Nahl: 10],

• And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And We send down from the sky pure water, that We may give life thereby to a dead land and give it to drink of that which We have created of cattle and many people﴾ [al-Furqan: 48–49],

• And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And We gave you to drink sweet water﴾ [al-Mursalat: 27],

and other verses besides these.

As for His saying here: ﴿If We willed, We could make it bitter﴾ [al-Waqi'ah: 70], meaning: if We willed to make it bitter, We would do so; but We made it sweet, fresh, its drink pleasant. We have already mentioned in surah al-Furqan that al-ujaj (bitter, salty water) is that which combines intense saltiness and bitterness.

What this noble verse includes, that if He willed He would make the water unfit for drinking, has had its meaning come in other verses, such as His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Say: Have you considered, if your water should sink away into the earth, who then would bring you flowing water?﴾ [al-Mulk: 30], and His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And We sent down water from the sky in measure, and We caused it to settle in the earth, and indeed, We are able to take it away﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 18]. This is because taking the water away, making it sink deep, or making it bitter — none of these reach the point of making it drinkable; all of them, in meaning, are alike in the common factor of preventing the drinking of water. These mentioned verses indicate the intense need of creation for their Creator, as you see.

His saying, exalted is He, in this noble verse: ﴿Is it you who bring it down from the rain-cloud﴾ [al-Waqi'ah: 69], indicates that all the water that is stored in the earth, flowing from springs, wells and the like, its origin is entirely from the rain-cloud, and that Allah caused it to settle in the earth and stored it there for His creation.

The meaning indicated by this verse has come clarified in other verses, such as His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And We sent down from the sky water in measure, and We caused it to settle in the earth﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 18], and His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Have you not seen that Allah sends down water from the sky and makes it flow as springs in the earth?﴾ [al-Zumar: 21]. We have already mentioned this in surah al-Hijr in the discussion of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And We sent down from the sky water and gave it to you to drink, and you are not its keepers﴾ [al-Hijr: 22], and in surah Saba' in the discussion of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿He knows what enters into the earth and what emerges from it﴾ [Saba': 2].

His saying, exalted is He, in this noble verse: ﴿so why do you not give thanks?﴾ [al-Waqi'ah: 70]: here "fa-lawla" means "halla" (why not), and it is a particle of tahdid (urging), which is a request with urging and exhortation. The meaning is that they are asked to give thanks for this great Benefactor, with urging and exhortation.

Know that gratitude (shukr) is attributed to the servant towards his Lord, and to the Lord towards His servant.

The gratitude of the servant to his Lord is summarized in using all His blessings in what pleases Him, exalted is He. The gratitude for the blessing of the eye is not to look through it except at what pleases the One who created it; and likewise for all the limbs. The gratitude for the blessing of wealth is to establish within it the commands of one's Lord, while also being thankful in heart and tongue. The gratitude of the servant to his Lord has come in many verses, such as His saying, exalted is He here: ﴿so why do you not give thanks?﴾ [al-Waqi'ah: 70], and His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And give thanks to Me and do not be ungrateful to Me﴾ [al-Baqarah: 152], and verses of similar kind are many and well known.

As for the gratitude of the Lord to His servant, it is that He rewards him with a great reward for his little deed. Among this is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And whoever volunteers good, then indeed Allah is Appreciative and Knowing﴾ [al-Baqarah: 158], and His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, our Lord is Forgiving and Appreciative﴾ [Fatir: 34], and other verses besides these.

Linguistic note

Know that the root sh-k-r transitively reaches the blessing at times, and the Benefactor at other times. If it is transitive to the blessing, it reaches it directly without a preposition, as in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿My Lord, enable me to be grateful for Your blessing which You have bestowed upon me﴾ [al-Naml: 19]. If it is transitive to the Benefactor, it reaches Him by the preposition lam, as in your saying: "We praise Allah and we give thanks to Him" (nashkuru lahu). It does not come in the Qur'an transitive except with lam, as in His saying: ﴿And give thanks to Me and do not be ungrateful to Me﴾ [al-Baqarah: 152], and His saying: ﴿Give thanks to Me and to your parents﴾ [Luqman: 14], and His saying: ﴿And give thanks to Allah, if it is Him that you worship﴾ [al-Nahl: 114], and His saying: ﴿So seek provision from Allah, and worship Him, and give thanks to Him; to Him you will be returned﴾ [al-'Ankabut: 17], and other verses besides these.

This is the eloquent Arabic usage, and its transitivity to the object without lam is a valid usage, not a grammatical error. Among this is the saying of Abu Nukhaylah:

"I thank you, for gratitude is the rope of him who is god-fearing, / and not everyone to whom you have given a blessing repays it."

And the saying of Jamil ibn Mu'mar:

"O my two friends, halt today until you greet / the one with sweet teeth and fragrant breath.
For if you two turn aside from me for an hour, / I will thank you both until I am hidden in my grave."

These verses of surah al-Waqi'ah have shown that the joining of the answer of "law" with lam and its absence are both permissible, because He, exalted is He, said: ﴿If We willed, We could make it debris﴾ [al-Waqi'ah: 65] with lam, then He said: ﴿If We willed, We could make it bitter﴾ [al-Waqi'ah: 70] without it.

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Have you considered the fire which you kindle?﴾ ﴿Is it you who produced its tree, or are We the Producer?﴾ ﴿We made it a reminder and a provision for the travellers in the wilderness.﴾

His saying, ﴿which you kindle﴾ [al-Waqi'ah: 71], means: which you light, from their saying: awra al-nar (he struck the fire and lit it) when he struck it (to produce sparks) and kindled it. The meaning is: Have you considered the fire which you kindle from the tree? Is it you who produced its tree, which is kindled from it, i.e., brought it into existence from non-existence?

The answer which has no other answer is: It is You, our Lord, who produced its tree, and we have no power over that. Then it is said: How do you deny resurrection when you know that He who produced the tree of fire and brought fire out of it is capable of everything?

What this noble verse includes, namely that the creation of fire is among the proofs of resurrection, is made clear in Ya-Sin in His saying: ﴿Say: He will give them life who produced them the first time, and He is Knowing of every creation.﴾ ﴿He who made for you from the green tree fire, and thereupon you kindle [from it].﴾ [Ya-Sin: 79-80]. His saying at the end of Ya-Sin, ﴿you kindle﴾ [Ya-Sin: 80], is the meaning of His saying in al-Waqi'ah, ﴿which you kindle﴾ [al-Waqi'ah: 71]. And His saying in the Ya-Sin verse, ﴿He who made for you from the green tree fire﴾ [Ya-Sin: 80], following His saying, ﴿He will give them life who produced them the first time﴾ [Ya-Sin: 79], is clear evidence that the creation of fire is among the proofs of resurrection. His saying here, ﴿Is it you who produced its tree﴾ [al-Waqi'ah: 72], means the tree from which fire is kindled, such as al-markh and al-'affar. And among the proverbs of the Arabs: "In every tree there is fire, and seek fire from al-markh and al-'affar," because al-markh and al-'affar are the trees most productive in extracting fire from them: they take a stick of al-markh and fix to it a piece of al-'affar, and fire comes out between the two. It is said: every tree has fire in it except al-'innab.

His saying, ﴿We made it a reminder﴾ [al-Waqi'ah: 73], means: We remind people by it in the abode of this world when they sense the intensity of its heat, that is, the fire of the Hereafter, which is more intense in heat, so that they may refrain from the deeds which necessitate entry into the Fire. It is authentically reported from him (ﷺ) that the heat of the Fire of the Hereafter is multiplied over the heat of the fire of this world seventy times, so it exceeds it by sixty-nine times, each one of which is like the heat of the fire of this world.

His saying, Exalted is He, ﴿and a provision for the travellers in the wilderness﴾ [al-Waqi'ah: 73], means: a benefit for those who dwell in the qiwa' of the earth, which is the empty, desolate wasteland in which no one is present, and they are the travellers, because they benefit greatly from the fire in warming themselves, lighting, and preparing their food.

It has been established in the principles of jurisprudence that among the impediments to considering the concept of contrary implication (mafhum al-mukhalafa) is that the wording is given for the purpose of favour (imtinan). By this you know that "for the travellers" is not considered a restrictive concept, because it was said for the sake of favour, meaning that it is also a provision for those other than the travellers who are present among the inhabited places. Every thing that is empty of people is called aqwa, so a man who is in an empty place is said to be aqwa, and a dwelling when emptied of its people is said to be aqwat.

From this is the saying of Nabigha Dhubyani:

O abode of Mayya at al-'Aliya and al-Sanad, it has become empty, and the ancient ages have lingered over it.

And the saying of 'Antara:

Greetings to you from a ruin whose traces have grown old, emptied and desolate after Umm al-Haytham.

It has been said that al-muqwin means the hungry, and other things have been said, but what the majority hold is what we have mentioned.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 56, verse 75:

The words of the Most High: ﴿So I swear by the positions of the stars﴾ ﴿and indeed it is a mighty oath, if you only knew﴾.

We have already discussed this in the beginning of Surat an-Najm.

⁕ ⁕ ⁕

The author said in (Daf' Iham al-Idtirab 'an Ayat al-Kitab):

(p-408) In the name of Allah, the Entirely Merciful, the Especially Merciful.

Surat al-Waqi'ah

The words of the Most High: ﴿So I swear by the positions of the stars﴾.

This implies that He did not swear by this oath, while the words of the Most High: ﴿and indeed it is a mighty oath, if you only knew﴾ [56], indicate the opposite of that.

The answer is in two ways:

The first: that the negating "la" (no) has its negation linked to the speech of the disbelievers, so its meaning is: the matter is not as the disbelievers who deny the Messenger claim. Accordingly, His words "I swear" are a fresh, independent affirmation.

The second: that the particle "la" is redundant (ṣilah, a filler particle), and we have promised to explain this with its evidences in combining the words of the Most High: ﴿I do not swear by this city﴾ [90], with the words of the Most High: ﴿and this secure city﴾ [At-Tin: 3].

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 56, verse 95:

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, this is the certain truth.﴾ ﴿So exalt by the name of your Lord, the Mighty.﴾

In this noble verse, Allah, Exalted is He, informs, and confirms His information, that this Great Qur'an is the certain truth, and then commands His Prophet, after that, to glorify the name of his Lord, the Mighty.

What this verse contains, Allah, Majestic and Exalted, mentioned at the end of Surah al-Haqqah, in His saying describing the Qur'an: ﴿And indeed, it is a regret upon the disbelievers.﴾ ﴿And indeed, it is the certain truth.﴾ ﴿So exalt by the name of your Lord, the Mighty.﴾ [69:50-52], and "al-haqq" is "al-yaqin" (the certainty).

We have already stated that the idafah (annexation) of a thing to itself, with the difference of the two wordings, is an Arabic stylistic usage, and we mentioned how frequently it occurs in the Qur'an and in the speech of the Arabs. Among its occurrences in the Qur'an is His saying: ﴿And the abode of the Hereafter﴾ [Yusuf: 109], where "ladar" (the abode) is the Hereafter itself; and His saying: ﴿And the evil plotting﴾ [Fatir: 43], where the plotting is itself the evil, as is shown by His saying after it: ﴿And evil plotting does not beset anyone except its own people﴾ [Fatir: 43].

And His saying: ﴿from the jugular vein﴾ [Qaf: 16], where "al-habl" (the vein) is "al-warid" (the jugular), and His saying: ﴿the month of Ramadan﴾ [al-Baqarah: 185], where "al-shahr" (the month) is Ramadan.

A parallel to this in the speech of the Arabs is the saying of Imru' al-Qays:

"Like a virgin of the cloistered, her whiteness mixed with yellowness, nourished by the water of a stream not diluted."

Here "al-bikr" (the virgin) is "al-muqanah" (the cloistered).

And the saying of 'Antarah:

"And a long, flowing coat of mail, I tore open its folds with the sword, defending the reality, a marked one."

Because his intended meaning by "al-mishakk" here is the coat of mail itself, as is shown by his saying: "I tore open its folds," meaning the coat of mail. Although the original meaning of "al-mishakk" in the lexicon is the strap with which the coat of mail is fastened, the strap cannot be intended in this verse of 'Antarah. This differs from what the author of Taj al-'Arus supposed. Rather, 'Antarah's intended meaning of "al-mishakk" is the coat of mail, and he annexed it to "al-sabighah," which is the coat of mail, as we have mentioned. To this points what they mentioned in the chapter on the proper noun, which he set out in the Khulasah with his saying:

"And if the two are single, annex, definitively; otherwise, make the second follow the one it is attached to."

Because the annexation mentioned is an annexation of a thing to itself with the difference of the two wordings. We have made clear in our book "Daf' Iham al-Idtirab 'an Ayat al-Kitab" that his saying in the Khulasah:

"A noun is not annexed to what is one with it in meaning; interpret it if it occurs in a way that gives a false impression."

What appears to us from surveying the Qur'an and Arabic is that this is an Arabic stylistic usage, that the difference between the two wordings is sufficient for distinguishing the annexed and the annexed-to, and that there is no need for interpretation given how frequently this occurs in the Qur'an and in Arabic.

This is supported by their explicit statement that annexing a noun to a title is obligatory if both are single, as in "Sa'id Kurz," because what must be interpreted cannot be the obligatory form, as you see. So its being a stylistic usage is more evident.

His saying: ﴿So exalt by the name of your Lord, the Mighty﴾ [al-Waqi'ah: 96]. Tasbih (glorification): its root meaning is distancing from evil, and the glorification of Allah and His transcendence above everything unbefitting His perfection and majesty. This transcendence is obligatory for Him in His essence, His names, His attributes, and His actions. The apparent meaning is that the ba' in His saying ﴿by the name of your Lord﴾ [al-Waqi'ah: 96] is attached to the direct object. We have already presented, in Surah Maryam, in discussing His saying: ﴿And shake toward you the trunk of the palm tree﴾ [Maryam: 25], many proofs from the Qur'an and other sources for the attachment of the ba' to the object to which the verb reaches directly, as in His saying: ﴿And shake toward you the trunk of the palm tree﴾ [Maryam: 25], and the meaning is: shake the trunk of the palm tree.

His saying: ﴿And whoever intends therein deviation by wrongdoing﴾ [al-Hajj: 25], meaning deviation, up to the end of what we have presented of the many proofs. Accordingly, the meaning is: glorify the name of your Lord, the Mighty, as His saying above clarifies: ﴿Exalt the name of your Lord, the Most High﴾ [al-A'la: 1].

Al-Qurtubi said: "The name here means the named (al-musamma), i.e., glorify your Lord." The use of "the name" to mean "the named" is well known in the speech of the Arabs, and among it is the saying of Labid:

"Until the year is complete, then peace be upon you both; and whoever weeps a full year has made an excuse."

In my view, it does not follow that "the name" here means "the named," since the intended meaning may be the name itself. The names of Allah have been distorted by some people, and others have declared them free of everything unbefitting. Allah described them as reaching the utmost beauty, and in that is the most complete declaration of their transcendence, since they encompass His noble attributes. This is in His saying: ﴿And to Allah belong the most beautiful names, so call upon Him by them﴾ [al-A'raf: 180], and His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Whichever you call, to Him belong the most beautiful names﴾ [al-Isra': 110].

We do not wish to mention the speech of the theologians concerning the name and the named, whether the name is the named or not, because our purpose here is to explain the meaning of the verse, and knowledge is with Allah, Exalted is He.
